sections.changelog:
Added

  • **Relevance now weights rare, distinctive words (IDF).** A word that appears in almost every product counts for far less than a rare model or part name, so a common word can no longer drag unrelated items to the top. On by default; toggle on the Relevance tab.
  • **Exact title / SKU match jumps to the top.** A product whose name or SKU is exactly the query is promoted above merely high-scoring partial matches. Adjustable on the Relevance tab.
  • **Bestseller boost (WooCommerce).** Among equally relevant matches, better-selling products are gently lifted, read straight from the product lookup table. Capped so it never outranks a clearly better match; 0 = off.
  • **Understands Russian out of the box.** A bundled synonym and brand-spelling dictionary (батарея / аккумулятор / АКБ, дисплей / экран, айфон / iPhone, сяоми / Xiaomi and more) works with no setup, plus cross-script transliteration so a query in one alphabet reaches products written in the other (samsung ↔ самсунг). Each group only fires when the query uses one of its words, so an unrelated catalog is never affected. All on by default.
  • **Price in the query becomes a filter (WooCommerce).** "чехол до 1000", "ноутбук от 30000" and "5000-10000" narrow results to the budget; if the filter would empty the results it is dropped automatically so nothing is hidden.
  • **Single-character models stay searchable.** A lone digit such as the "5" in "iPhone 5" is now indexed instead of being dropped by the two-character minimum (reindex to apply).
  • **Automatic index maintenance.** A lightweight scheduled pass re-indexes anything modified since the last run, catching bulk imports and tools that bypass the usual save hooks. The Index tab also flags when the index has fallen far behind the published content. Completion hooks for WP All Import and the native WooCommerce CSV importer are recognised, and a `mvweb_ss_reindex_hooks` filter lets any importer register its own.
  • **`wp mvweb-ss eval`** — run a saved query→expected-top set and diff the current ranking against it, so a relevance change can be told apart from a regression before it ships.

Changed

  • **Coverage counts concepts, not words.** A word and its synonym or transliteration now count as one covered concept, so an item matching a word and its synonym no longer unfairly out-ranks a genuine two-word match.

Fixed

  • A synonym or dictionary entry that is a plain number (e.g. a model like "1660") no longer causes a fatal error on search.
  • Popularity and click ranking boosts now sort correctly on all MySQL/MariaDB versions.
  • The automatic index maintenance no longer skips items when a bulk import stamps the same modification time on more than one batch of products (keyset cursor by time and ID).
  • A price filter in the query now also applies to typo-corrected and wrong-layout retries, so those never return products outside the requested budget.
